issues.description: The Bitmap24 API is inconsistent in the template repository: Bitmap24.hpp declares a method named 'write(const std::string&)', but the implementation defines 'Bitmap24::save(const std::string&)' and client code (main.cpp) calls bitmap.save(...). This name/signature mismatch prevents the template from compiling and confuses students which method to implement/use. The solution repository uses 'save(...)', matching the implementation and usage, so the template header is the outlier.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the header, implementation, and callers consistent. Prefer the existing implementation/usage in main and the solution: change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'void write(const std::string &i_filename);' to 'void save(const std::string &i_filename);' (or alternatively rename the implementation and all callers to 'write'). Update any references accordingly so the declaration, definition, and calls match.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 file-writing API name is inconsistent between template and solution/implementation. In the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the class declares a method named write(const std::string&), while the implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines Bitmap24::save(const std::string&). The solution header uses save(...) matching the implementation. This mismatch in the template prevents students from mapping the header to the implementation and causes compilation errors (main.cpp calls bitmap.save(...), but the template header exposes write(...)).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API name consistent. Rename the template header declaration write(...) to save(...) to match the implementation and the solution (or alternatively rename the implementation to write(...)). Ensure main.cpp, the header, and the .cpp implementation all use the same identifier (preferably save(const std::string&)).
